AboutPage.title: About — InferCheck
AboutPage.description: Why InferCheck exists, who built it, and how to report outdated or missing provider information.
AboutPage.ogDescription: Built by Carlo Nölle (CodeAttack, Cologne), who answers the same AI provider and GDPR questions in every project for EU companies.
AboutPage.heading: About this directory
AboutPage.subtitle: A neutral, sourced reference for AI inference compliance — built because no such resource existed.
AboutPage.whyExistsPara1: I build AI solutions for companies in the EU. In every project the same questions come up before the first line of code: Where does the data go at inference time? Is there a DPA we can actually sign? Does the provider train on our inputs? Is there an EU-only routing option?
AboutPage.whyExistsPara2: There is no single place to look these up. You dig through privacy policies, data processing addenda and support docs — for every provider, every time. Many teams therefore default to expensive enterprise contracts (Azure OpenAI, IBM Watsonx). Not because the models are better, but because the compliance paperwork is already done.
AboutPage.whyExistsPara3: This directory is the resource I wanted. It presents structured, sourced facts — not a provider's own marketing copy, not a law firm's generic checklist — so you can make a defensible provider selection and move on.
AboutPage.whoBuiltPara1: I'm Carlo Nölle from Cologne. I run CodeAttack, where I build AI solutions for companies in the EU. I'm a senior software engineer, an iSAQB-certified software architect and an AWS Solutions Architect.
AboutPage.whoBuiltPara2: Neither I nor CodeAttack has a financial relationship with any provider listed here. No provider pays for an entry, and my work at CodeAttack has no influence on the data. Compliance metadata reflects publicly verifiable information with source links — if something is wrong or has changed, I want to know.
AboutPage.dataMaintenancePara1: Every provider entry is a flat JSON file stored in the public GitHub repository. Each field has a source URL. Entries are researched with AI assistance and reviewed over time. Every entry is labelled as an AI draft or as manually verified, together with its date, so you can judge how reliable and how fresh the information is before acting on it.
AboutPage.dataMaintenancePara2: Provider compliance terms change — sometimes quietly. If you spot something outdated or missing, the best thing you can do is open an issue on GitHub. The issue template asks for the specific field that changed and a link to the source document. That keeps updates auditable and reviewable before they go into the directory.
AboutPage.seenChangePara: If a provider has updated their DPA, changed their data residency terms, launched EU-only routing, or anything else relevant to GDPR compliance — please file a GitHub issue. The structured template takes under two minutes and helps keep this resource accurate for everyone.
AboutPage.githubNote: A GitHub account is required to submit. You can also browse
AboutPage.notLegalAdviceBody: The directory presents facts, not compliance judgments. Always verify with the provider directly and consult legal counsel before relying on this for procurement decisions.
AboutPage.notPaidBody: No provider has paid to appear here or to influence how their data is presented.
AboutPage.notCurrentBody: Provider terms change. The date on each entry tells you when it was last researched or, for manually verified entries, last confirmed against source documents.
AboutPage.codeAttackHeading: Planning to use AI in your company?
AboutPage.codeAttackPara1: Through CodeAttack I build AI agents, automations and smart reporting for mid-sized companies and SMEs that have no AI team of their own. At a fixed price, in production, GDPR-compliant.
AboutPage.codeAttackPara2: The questions this directory answers come up in every one of these projects. Where the data requires it, the solution runs in the EU or on your own servers, optionally with a self-hosted model. I measure quality on your real cases before go-live and hand over with documentation, so you are not locked in.
AboutPage.codeAttackPara3: A good place to start is the AI Potential Check. If you already have a proposal from an agency, I give a second opinion on its scope, architecture, data protection and price.

PrivacyPage.title: Privacy Policy — InferCheck
PrivacyPage.description: Privacy policy for InferCheck. We use Vercel for hosting, self-hosted Umami for anonymous analytics, and Neon Postgres in the EU for our database.
PrivacyPage.ogDescription: How InferCheck processes data: Vercel hosting, anonymous Umami analytics, Neon Postgres EU database.
PrivacyPage.heading: Privacy Policy
PrivacyPage.legalNote: The legally binding version of this privacy policy is the <german>German version (Datenschutzerklärung)</german>. This English translation is provided for convenience only.
PrivacyPage.introText: This privacy policy informs you about the nature, scope, and purpose of the processing of personal data on this website. Personal data is any data by which you can be personally identified. We take the protection of your personal data seriously.
PrivacyPage.controllerText: The controller responsible for data processing on this website within the meaning of the GDPR is:
PrivacyPage.hostingText: This website is hosted by Vercel Inc., 340 Pine Street, Suite 900, San Francisco, CA 94104, USA. When you visit this website, Vercel processes technical connection data including IP addresses, browser type, operating system, referrer URL, and timestamps. This processing is necessary for the technical provision of the website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR — legitimate interest). Vercel acts as a data processor under a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with us. Data may be transferred to the USA under the EU–US Data Privacy Framework (adequacy decision, July 2023). For more information see <link>vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy</link>.
PrivacyPage.analyticsText: This website uses Umami, a privacy-friendly, open-source analytics software. Umami is self-hosted on a Hetzner VPS in Frankfurt, Germany (EU). Umami does not use cookies and does not collect any personally identifiable information. It tracks anonymous, aggregated page views and visitor counts without cross-site tracking. No data is shared with third parties. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in understanding general usage patterns to improve the website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Because no personal data is processed, no opt-out is required; however, standard browser privacy settings and ad blockers will prevent Umami tracking if desired.
PrivacyPage.databaseText: The model catalog powering this directory's search functionality is stored in a PostgreSQL database provided by Neon Inc. The database is located in the AWS eu-central-1 region (Frankfurt, Germany). The database stores only publicly available information about AI providers and models — no user data, accounts, or personal data of visitors. Neon acts as a data processor under a Data Processing Agreement. For more information see <link>neon.tech/privacy</link>.
PrivacyPage.githubText: This website links to GitHub for submitting change requests and data corrections. When you open a GitHub issue, you interact directly with GitHub's platform (GitHub, Inc., 88 Colin P Kelly Jr St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA). GitHub processes data according to their own privacy policy. Submitting an issue is entirely voluntary. We use GitHub issues to maintain accuracy of directory data in a transparent, auditable way. See <link>docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement</link> for GitHub's privacy practices.
PrivacyPage.errorTrackingText: This website uses GlitchTip, an open-source error monitoring tool, to capture application errors and exceptions. GlitchTip is self-hosted on a Hetzner VPS in Frankfurt, Germany (EU) — the same infrastructure used for our analytics. Error reports may include technical information such as browser type, operating system, page URL, and a stack trace. This data is used solely to identify and fix software defects and is never shared with third parties. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in maintaining the reliability and security of the website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). For more information see <link>glitchtip.com</link>.
PrivacyPage.rightsText: Under the GDPR, you have the following rights regarding your personal data:
rightsList: Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR)
PrivacyPage.rightsContact: To exercise these rights, contact us at carlo@codeattack.io. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. The competent authority for Cologne is:
PrivacyPage.supervisoryAuthority: Landesbeauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit Nordrhein-Westfalen (LDI NRW), Postfach 20 04 44, 40102 Düsseldorf, Germany
PrivacyPage.cookiesText: This website does not use cookies for tracking or advertising. A session cookie may be set by the hosting infrastructure (Vercel) for technical routing purposes only. No persistent tracking cookies are set.
PrivacyPage.changesText: We may update this privacy policy from time to time. The current version is always available at this URL. Material changes will be reflected in the "last updated" date above.
